long_biography.plain_text:
Redken emerged from Paula Kent Meehan’s frustration with hair products that dried her fine hair and irritated her scalp during an early acting career. Working with hairdresser Jheri Redding, she turned a scientific interest in protein, moisture and natural pH into professional products and an education programme that taught stylists the chemistry behind them. By 1965, she had bought Redding’s interest and controlled the company.

Meehan paired product development with unusually disciplined distribution and finance. She defended salon-only sales, took Redken public, then led a $48.5 million buyout to return it to private ownership. Beyond the company, she created investment and marketing businesses and applied the same management scrutiny to philanthropy. She founded the Pet Care Foundation, organised adoption programmes and supported medical research and Beverly Hills cultural projects.

uncertainties.detail: The upstream record gives 23 September 1932, but its existing biography already gives 9 August 1931. The Los Angeles Times expressly reports 9 August 1931, while Modern Salon identifies 9 August as her birthday and confirms death at age 82 before that year's birthday. Day, month and year are therefore proposed as corrections; the derived upstream age fields are left untouched because they are system-managed.

UCLA identifies her birth name as Paula Jane Baer. Jane is proposed as the missing middle name. The established public identity Paula Kent Meehan is retained without trying to reconstruct every prior married or professional surname in the owner fields.

Meehan's historical founder and operator role is exceptionally well documented, but she sold Redken in 1993. UCLA mentions later investment and marketing companies without establishing which asset principally held or managed her wealth, so the current relationship remains Unknown under the schema's post-exit rule.

Meehan died before the current prominence of LinkedIn and Instagram, and no verified personal account or personal website was found. Her dedicated Wikipedia page and Redken's official founder-history page are proposed under their correct link types; no Forbes profile is proposed because the exact-profile check was negative.

The upstream Ancallia relationship is consistent with public evidence that Paula Meehan owned the same Feadship under its former name Dream Seeker in 1999. The vessel evidence is used only to strengthen identity resolution and is excluded from both biographies and classifications.

Cosmetics & beauty is the minimum useful active catalogue tag for Meehan's defining Redken ownership and operating role. Her philanthropy remains narrative context because generic philanthropy-domain tags are prohibited and no additional active tag passes the information-value test.
